turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so you have twenty-five minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?

Out of time. You asked for this meeting and I've been in the chair one minute, so you'll answer my question or I'm walking straight to the principal's office. Who decided on the zero, Hale, and before or after anyone heard from Owen?
Just say okay and I'll write it up as resolved. Okay?
No. You're trying to write this up as resolved before you've answered a single question, and I'm writing that down. Who decided on the zero, Hale?
I've answered that. If you're not going to tell me who decided on the zero, I'm going upstairs to the principal now.
Ms. Kalinowski. I need you to say okay.
You don't get an okay from me, Hale, not without a single answer. The principal's office is my next stop unless you tell me, right now, whether Owen was heard before that zero went in.
